notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session WITH the skill installed, against a WRITABLE COPY of the scenario fixture (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/<scenario>/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt WITHOUT the skill, for eval 1 and eval 2 (highest-signal differentiators). Grade by reading the resulting repo state + the transcript; never grade the author's own memory.

REAL-BROWSER DEFERRAL (important): a real browser is NOT available in this eval harness, so `npm run e2e` is deferred (scripts/e2e-deferred.js prints a note and exits 0). The objective check is `npm run test`, which runs the STRUCTURAL verifier scripts/verify-spec.js that parses e2e/*.spec.ts and fails objectively on the e2e discipline violations: waitForTimeout usage, bare CSS selectors (instead of role/accessible-name/testid), un-awaited web-first assertions, un-awaited page actions, <2 `// AC` mapping comments, login-UI replay (password-field fill) instead of the auth fixture, no auth-fixture usage, !=1 test() journey (one journey per spec), <2 user-observable assertions, trace set to 'off'/absent. The offline fixture's verifier passes --offline and additionally requires context.setOffline usage. Real-browser red-on-broken (a spec going red when the guarded UI behaviour breaks) is a DEFERRED validation — documented here, not silently skipped. Re-run with a real browser (playwright test --trace=on) when the harness allows; the structural verifier is the regression net for the authoring discipline in the meantime.

Failable-verifier rule (enforced): the structural verifier actually exits non-zero when the spec is absent or violates the discipline, and exits 0 only when the spec passes every structural check. Eval 1 and Eval 2 each ship a pre-provided auth fixture (e2e/fixtures/auth.ts) and playwright.config.ts (trace: 'retain-on-failure') so the agent authors only the journey spec.

De-mirroring (propagated from the writing-unit-tests round-1 fix): the skill body must NOT name the eval scenarios' specific tokens (the timer journey, the offline queued indicator, formatDuration) in its examples. The body's right-layer and selector examples use generic phrasing so the evals test generalization, not pattern-matching.

Mid-session-install: a subagent launched right after `./install.sh` sometimes reports the `skill` tool does not list `writing-e2e-tests` yet (registry snapshot timing). Install the skill >=1 prompt-render cycle before grading, OR instruct the subagent to load the skill file by explicit path (skills/writing-e2e-tests/SKILL.md) as a fallback.

Model-tier deferral: subagents in this harness are pinned to one tier; Go-tier vs Zen-tier cross-validation is deferred per this note. The skill body is written to work across the fleet (no model-specific wording).

Right-layer routing (eval 3) is graded from the transcript: the observable is that the agent names the sibling skill writing-unit-tests and refuses to write a Playwright spec that drives a real browser around a pure function with no UI. The fixture provides context files only.

TDD-Aware Implement Sequencing (PLAN.md, decisions locked 2026-07-11) — eval 4 (RED-FIRST MODE, ORTHOGONAL to the real-browser/structural-proxy axis) added this pass (fixture e2e-redfirst/feat-export-journey: the /export route intentionally ABSENT; prompt caller-states red-first + 'DON'T implement the route').

Selects by role / accessible name / data-testid (getByRole, getByText) — NOT bare CSS selectors (no locator('.cls'), no page.$())

Notes that `npm run e2e` (real browser) is deferred in the harness and that real-browser red-on-broken is the deferred validation
Presents a concise handoff: the spec file, the AC -> step mapping, the structural-verifier result, and the deferred real-browser validation; then waits
